title: Pure steam generators to EN 285 | Aquemi
meta: Pure steam generators for autoclaves and steam-in-place. Condensate meets WFI limits; non-condensable gases, dryness and superheat tested to EN 285.
headline: Pure steam generators
lead: Our pure steam generators supply sterilizers and steam-in-place with steam whose condensate meets Water for Injection (WFI) limits, and whose gas content, dryness and superheat are tested to EN 285.

blocks.caption: Pure steam · EN 285 and USP Pure Steam
blocks.note: EN 285 physical tests are made at the point of use, so header design matters as much as the generator. We test at the generator outlet at FAT and at the sterilizer at SAT.

rows.m: Double tube sheet exchanger on steam-heated units

blocks.caption: Feed water is preheated and degassed to remove non-condensable gases. Plant steam or electric heaters boil it in the evaporator. A separator removes droplets that carry endotoxins and solids. Pure steam leaves at a controlled pressure, and blowdown removes concentrated impurities.

items.q: Our sterilizer fails dryness tests. Is it the generator?
items.a: Often it is the header: long runs, missing traps or poor insulation produce wet steam at the point of use. We survey the distribution and the generator together.

items.q: What feed water does a pure steam generator need?
items.a: Purified Water or RO permeate, free of chlorine and low in silica. Feed quality determines blowdown rate and the cleaning interval.

items.q: Do you test to EN 285 at FAT?
items.a: Yes. We run the non-condensable gas, dryness and superheat tests on the generator outlet during FAT, then repeat them at the point of use during SAT.
